articles.title: Could the midterm results change the future of DC statehood?
articles.summary: The Democrats' midterm victories could revive the fight for DC statehood, but Senate rules and Republican opposition remain major obstacles.
articles.body:
Washington DC has spent decades fighting for the same congressional representation enjoyed by the 50 states, but the District's push for statehood has repeatedly stalled, largely because of Republican opposition in Congress.

But could the results of the 2026 midterm elections could give the movement a new opening?

The Democrats' victories in the House and Senate could put statehood legislation back on the congressional agenda, potentially giving advocates their best opportunity in years to advance the effort.

Candidates make history in race, gender and faith in 2026

Could Democrats put DC statehood back on the agenda?

Congress has broad authority over the District, including the power to review its budget, overturn local laws and intervene in city affairs. DC residents lack voting representation in either chamber, with just a nonvoting delegate in the House and no senators.

Democrats have historically been more supportive of statehood than Republicans. With control of both chambers upcoming, they will have greater influence over which proposals receive consideration.

The latest statehood legislation, the Washington DC Admission Act , was introduced in January 2025 by Eleanor Holmes Norton, the District's nonvoting representative. Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Maryland, introduced companion legislation in the Senate.

The proposal would make most of the District a state while maintaining a smaller federal district containing the White House, Capitol and other federal buildings.

The House has previously passed statehood legislation , voting 216-208 in favor in April 2021. However, the measure never received a final Senate vote.

Why DC statehood remains a difficult fight

Even with control of Congress, Democrats would face a significant obstacle in the Senate.

As of Thursday morning, Democrats had secured at least 54 Senate seats, with two races still undecided. That would give them a majority, but it would leave them short of the 60 votes generally needed to overcome a filibuster and advance major legislation.

Under current Senate rules, Democrats would need at least six additional votes from Republicans or other senators to reach that threshold.

Democrats could try to negotiate with Republicans for support, change Senate rules to eliminate the filibuster for statehood legislation or pursue another procedural approach, but each option would come with political challenges.

The House would also need to approve the legislation, and President Donald Trump would have to sign it into law. If he vetoed it, Congress would need a two-thirds majority in both the House and Senate to override him.

Republicans have generally opposed statehood, arguing that it would give Democrats an unfair political advantage. The District overwhelmingly votes Democratic, and becoming a state would give the District two U.S. senators and at least one voting House representative.

The Senate has never held a final floor vote on a DC statehood bill, despite the House approving one twice.

articles.title: Sanjay Singh hits back at Kharge's 'BJP's B-team' remark, says Congress 'helped BJP form governments' in several states
articles.summary: SULTANPUR: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh on Thursday hit back at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge over his 'BJP's B-team' remark,
articles.body: SULTANPUR: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh on Thursday hit back at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge over his 'BJP's B-team' remark, accusing Congress of repeatedly helping the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) form governments in several states through defections by its MLAs.Addressing a press conference in Sultanpur, Singh questioned the Congress's criticism of the AAP, alleging that its MLAs had repeatedly switched sides and joined the BJP in several states.Citing examples from Arunachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Goa, Karnataka and Madhya Pradesh, Singh alleged that Congress MLAs had defected to the BJP, facilitating the formation of BJP governments."In Arunachal Pradesh in 2016, the public voted for Congress Party. Yet, the entire Congress party and its MLAs defected to the BJP and formed a BJP government," he said.Referring to other states, Singh alleged that nine Congress MLAs switched to the BJP in Uttarakhand in 2016, 13 crossed over in Goa in 2017, 13 defected in Karnataka in 2019 and 22 joined the BJP in Madhya Pradesh in 2020."In Goa again in 2022, eight Congress MLAs broke away and joined the BJP. Across the entire country, the Congress party and its MLAs repeatedly defect in chunks to join the BJP and form their governments. Entire state units of the Congress cross over to the BJP--and today, you are questioning us?" he said.The AAP MP also cited the cases of party leaders, including Arvind Kejriwal, Manish Sisodia, Satyendar Jain and himself, who, he said, had gone to jail while fighting the BJP."The Aam Aadmi Party is that party whose topmost leader, Arvind Kejriwal, went to jail while serving as Chief Minister after fighting the BJP. Our Education Minister Manish Sisodia went to jail fighting the BJP; our Health Minister Satyendar Jain went to jail; I went to jail," Singh said."Can you name four major leaders of Congress Party who went to jail? Hemant Soren went to jail, leaders of the TMC went to jail, DMK leaders went to jail--tell us the names of four senior Congress leaders who went to jail! And yet, you have the audacity to question us?" he added.Singh further questioned the Congress over its electoral performance in several states, citing the periods during which the party had remained out of power in different parts of the country."In Uttar Pradesh, Congress has been out of power for 37 years. In Bihar, for 36 years. In West Bengal, for 54 years. In Tamil Nadu, for 59 years," he said, listing other states as well."Assess your own shortcomings! Look within yourselves! Across the country, you are the ones who strengthened the BJP, empowered them, and committed the crime of helping them form governments. And now you question the Aam Aadmi Party?" he said.Calling Congress the real 'BJP's B-team', Singh said the party had been losing elections in several states for decades and accused it of making baseless allegations against the AAP."The entire country is watching and knows who the real 'B-team' of the BJP is. It is Congress that facilitates BJP governments and has been losing elections for decades. In Gujarat, you have been losing elections for 31 years--AAP didn't even exist back then; why were you losing then?" he said.Singh further said the AAP government in Punjab, under Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, had delivered for the people and would return to power with a majority."Under the leadership of Bhagwant Mann ji, the Aam Aadmi Party government has delivered for the people of Punjab, and we will form the government there once again with a resounding, thumping majority," he said.On Wednesday, addressing the Congress' 'Insaaf Rally' in Sangrur, Kharge had accused the AAP government in Punjab of corruption and drug-related issues and alleged that public money was being sent from the state to Delhi."The Punjab government is a government of drugs and corruption. I have not seen such a corrupt government in my 60 years of public life. Money is being sent from here to Delhi.
